paper.core_task: Enhancing long-context State Space Models with dual-memory for internal and external knowledge.

contributions.name: A chunk-wise long-term memory mechanism for Mamba-based SSMs
contributions.author_claim_text: We introduce a chunk-wise long-term memory mechanism for Mamba-based SSMs. This architectural enhancement significantly mitigates the inherent forgetting problem for information within the input context.
contributions.description: Introduces a dynamic internal memory that partitions input into chunks to store state representations, mitigating information decay and improving in-context recall over long distances.

contributions.name: A pre-training methodology for integrating static external knowledge
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose a novel pre-training methodology to deeply integrate a static, pre-encoded external knowledge base into the model's learning process.
contributions.description: Proposes a method to pre-train the model to fuse a static, pre-encoded external knowledge base (e.g., embeddings) directly, avoiding the cost of concatenating raw text.

contributions.name: A unified dual-memory architecture and staged training system
contributions.author_claim_text: We combine these advancements in our Plastic Unified Memory Network (PUM-Net). We demonstrate that the resulting synergy from the deep integration of both internal and external memory systems leads to substantial improvements.
contributions.description: Combines the internal and external memory systems into a unified architecture and introduces a staged parallel computation training scheme for efficient end-to-end learning.

novelty_claims.text: The chunk-wise internal memory addresses the inherent limitations of SSMs in retaining information over long sequences, improving in-sequence recall.
PUM-Net's approach to integrating external knowledge into the model's learning process is novel and could have significant implications for long-context modeling tasks.
